title: Extinguishers and gas cylinders — handling, transport and service
verdict: I would not sign this and I would not send a crew out on it. It is the strongest of the ten in its citations — I checked s 291's lettering, s 289, s 299(2), ss 309/310/312, s 60(2), ss 68 and 69 against the current Queensland Reg, confirmed that Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) Part 8 Division 3 genuinely is "Electrical work on or near energised electrical equipment", and confirmed AS 2030.1:2026 and AS 2030.5:2026 are real editions that superseded the 2009 versions on 25 June 2026. It is also honest in places most statements are not: it says out loud that the discharge bay does not remove the hazard, that a 16 kg cut is the company's number and not the law's, that a valve cap does not make a full cylinder safe. None of that saves it. It declares s 291(o), movement of powered mobile plant, as a high risk construction work category that applies to this job, requires an LF forklift licence in its training list, walks the technician through a basement carpark and up a steep basement ramp with a loaded trolley — and then contains not one hazard entry and not one control anywhere about being struck by a vehicle or a forklift. It names oxygen displacement "in any low point it drains into" and then keeps every single control inside the bay, so the pit the CO2 runs into is named and abandoned. It names discharge noise and hearing damage in an extreme-risk step that carries eleven controls and no hearing protection at all. It tells the technician to vent a discharge manifold without saying where the agent goes, inside a sealed agent room. It lets "or 000" stand as a confined space rescue plan in the same breath as making the retrieval line conditional on the shape of the hole, which authorises entry into a space nobody can pull you out of. And in the very first assessment step it names a stripped neck thread and an unidentifiable agent as hazards and never tells anybody what to do about either — a defect that surfaces four steps later as a still-pressurised cylinder going into a vice. Three of those are ways a person dies. Fix them, plus the smaller citation and level faults below, and I will read it again.

blocking.field: hrcw[4] and training[12] vs steps[5].hazards, steps[6].hazards / steps[6].controls, steps[7].hazards
blocking.problem: The statement declares powered mobile plant as an applicable HRCW category and then never controls it. hrcw[4] asserts s 291(o) — "is carried out in an area at a workplace in which there is any movement of powered mobile plant" — applies to this activity (I confirmed that quote is exact). training[12] requires "High risk work licence class LF where a forklift is used to move cylinder pallets in the workshop". steps[5].hazards[3] walks the technician "through a crowded plant room or a basement carpark"; steps[6] has him at an open tailgate; steps[7].hazards[3] names "a steep basement ramp". Across all twelve steps there is no hazard entry for being struck by a vehicle or a forklift, and no control of any level establishing vehicle/pedestrian separation, an exclusion zone, cones, a spotter, or where the ute may stand. The whenRequired scope-out paragraph names only work above 2 m, cutting or grinding, and supply-side electrical work — it does not send this hazard to the traffic-lone statement, so the crew reading this one is told the category applies and is handed nothing. A technician crouched at a tailgate in a live basement carpark, or crossing a workshop floor a forklift is working, is the most likely way somebody on this job is killed by something that is not a cylinder.
blocking.fix: Add to steps[6].hazards: "Struck by a reversing vehicle, or by a forklift moving cylinder pallets, while loading, unloading or wheeling a cylinder in a carpark, loading dock or workshop." Insert as steps[6].controls[2], level engineering, above the existing administrative block: "Park so the tailgate opens to a wall, a kerb or a closed bay — never into a live lane or a reversing path. Cones or a barrier out around the working side of the vehicle before the tailgate drops, hazard lights on for the whole load, and hi-vis on from the moment you step out." Insert as steps[6].controls[3], level isolate: "In the workshop, cylinder pallets move by forklift only inside a barriered forklift lane that a technician does not cross, or with the floor between the racks and the bench cleared of people first. Operator and technician confirm eye contact before either one moves." Insert as steps[5].controls[4], level administrative: "In an occupied carpark or loading dock, get the building to close the bay or the aisle you are working in. If they will not, you work behind cones, you stand out of every reversing path, and you do not wheel a loaded trolley across a live lane."

blocking.problem: steps[8].hazards[3] reads "Oxygen displacement in the bay or in any low point it drains into". Every control in the step stops at the bay wall: controls[1] "Discharge outdoors or in the purpose-built bay"; controls[3] "Bunded bay with extraction running; discharge downwind and clear of air intakes, windows and pedestrian routes"; controls[6] gas detection "worn on the person in the bay and checked by the person outside". CO2, argon and inert blends are heavier than air. They leave the bay door or the outdoor discharge point along the ground and settle in the pit, sump, drain chamber, stairwell, lift well or basement ramp downhill of it. Nothing in the step identifies those low points, keeps anyone out of them, or requires them to be tested before somebody walks back in. The document itself names the mechanism and then hands the crew no control for it — the person who dies is someone who was never near the discharge.
blocking.fix: Insert as steps[8].controls[5], level engineering, immediately after the bund drain control: "Before the first pin comes out on any CO2 or inert-gas discharge, walk the fall of the ground from the bay door or the outdoor discharge point and identify every pit, sump, drain chamber, stairwell, lift well, basement ramp and below-grade doorway the agent can run into. Barricade and sign each one before the discharge and leave it barricaded until the bay has been ventilated and cleared." Follow it with an administrative control: "Nobody enters any of those low points afterwards until the atmosphere in it has been tested, at the bottom, on the instrument that reads the agent you discharged. An oxygen reading above 19.5% does not clear a low point after a CO2 discharge — it is the same trap the emergency section already warns about."

blocking.problem: controls[3] requires "Retrieval harness and line on the entrant, anchored outside the space, wherever the access shape allows one to be used and hauled" — so where the shape does not allow one, there is none. controls[7] then accepts a rescue plan of "haul on the retrieval line, or 000 with the location, the access route and the agent named". The same control opens by requiring that the plan "must get the entrant out without the standby person going in", and then offers a second limb that does not get the entrant out at all. Read together they authorise entry into an oxygen-deficient or agent-contaminated space with no means of retrieval and no stop rule, and the crew will take the easier limb. A technician who drops in an argon-flooded or CO2-loaded pit with no line on him, and a standby correctly told not to enter, is dead well before a brigade BA crew is rigged and down the hatch. The emergency section repeats the same fallback rather than closing it.
blocking.fix: Insert as steps[3].controls[1], level isolate, immediately under the eliminate control: "No retrieval line that can actually be hauled through that access, and no BA-equipped rescue arranged and standing on site, means no entry. The cylinder comes out through the hatch on a rope from outside, or the job is rebooked with a rescue crew. '000 will come' is not a rescue plan for a space nobody can pull you out of." Amend controls[7] to read: "...and it must get the entrant out without the standby person going in: haul on the retrieval line, and 000 called at the same time with the location, the access route and the agent named. 000 is what happens as well as the haul, never instead of it." Make the same change to the PERSON DOWN paragraph in the emergency section.

blocking.problem: The control reads "Vent the manifold and confirm the manifold gauge reads zero before the union is cracked. Stand to the side of the union, not over it." It never says where the vented agent goes. This step is carried out inside the protected space — normally a sealed, gas-tight, poorly ventilated agent room — and deliberately releasing the trapped manifold charge of CO2, nitrogen, argon or an inert blend into that room is an oxygen-displacement and CO2 event in the room the technician is standing in. steps[4] carries no ventilation control, no gas-monitor control and no second-person control of its own; its only respiratory-adjacent line is controls[6] "face shield if the manifold has not been proven at zero", which addresses blowback, not atmosphere. The atmosphere controls all sit in steps[2], a card the technician scrolled past, and a crew reads down the step it is on. The step also names "Residual agent in the manifold blowing back" as hazards[3] and controls only the mechanical half of it.
blocking.fix: Insert as steps[4].controls[2], level engineering, before "Cylinder stays strapped in its bracket": "Vent the manifold through a hose run out of the room, or with the room's mechanical ventilation running and the door held open on a hold-open that releases on alarm. A manifold is never cracked to atmosphere in a sealed agent room with the door shut." Insert as steps[4].controls[5], level administrative: "Gas monitor matched to that agent on your collar and reading, and the second person at the door, before the manifold vent is opened. Walk out on the first alarm and let the room clear before you go back to the union."

blocking.field: steps[2].hazards[3] vs the eleven controls at steps[2].controls[0]–[10]
blocking.problem: steps[2].hazards[3] is "Discharge noise causing hearing damage and disorientation". The step rates initialRisk extreme and carries eleven controls — none is hearing protection, none mentions noise, and the step has no ppe-level control at all. ppe[4] confines "Class 5 earmuffs or plugs to AS/NZS 1270" to "discharge testing". The whole premise of this step is that a charged bank can discharge while you are standing at it — that is why the actuator comes off. A CO2 or inert bank discharging into a plant room is well over 130 dB at the nozzle: instantaneous permanent hearing loss, and disorientation in a room the technician then has to find the door of while the agent is filling it. The document names the injury and then leaves it entirely uncontrolled, which is worse than not naming it, because the crew reads the hazard line and assumes something below it handles it.
blocking.fix: Add as the last control in steps[2], level ppe: "Class 5 hearing protection to AS/NZS 1270 in your pocket and on your head before you go inside a protected space that has a charged bank in it, and kept on for the whole time the actuator is off or being handled. If that bank lets go you do not get a chance to put them on." Amend ppe[4] to read "...for discharge testing and for any entry to a protected space with a charged gaseous bank — a CO2 discharge is over 110 dB and a bank discharging into a plant room is louder again."

blocking.field: steps[1].hazards[2] and steps[1].hazards[4] vs steps[1].controls[0]; consequence at steps[9].hazards[4] / steps[9].controls[3]
blocking.problem: steps[1] names "Damaged valve, bent actuator or stripped neck thread" (hazards[2]) and "Unknown or mixed agent" (hazards[4]) and controls neither. The eliminate control at controls[0] condemns only for "Pitted, bulged, fire-damaged, arc-struck or out of test" — thread and valve damage is not on that list, and an unidentifiable agent is not on it either. Nothing else in the step tells the technician what to do when they find one. The failure surfaces four steps later: steps[9].hazards[4] names "Stripped or corroded neck threads letting go" and the only control offered is controls[3], "Cylinder clamped in the vice with the body pointing away from people and away from the door" — which manages the direction a valve flies, not whether it flies. A still-pressurised cylinder with a stripped neck thread should be condemned at the bracket and never reach the vice. The unknown-agent gap is separately dangerous: an unidentified agent may be halon or an HFC that must be recovered under the Commonwealth scheme rather than vented, which the statement is otherwise strict about.
blocking.fix: Extend steps[1].controls[0] to read: "Condemn on the spot. Pitted, bulged, fire-damaged, arc-struck, out of test, a bent or seized valve or actuator, or a damaged, corroded or stripped neck thread means it never gets pressurised again — and a cylinder with a damaged neck thread is never taken to the vice with pressure still in it. Recover or discharge the contents by the right route for that agent, drill or stamp it out of service, and take it away so nobody puts it back on the bracket." Add as a new steps[1].controls[5], level administrative: "A cylinder whose agent cannot be identified from the shoulder stamp, the label and the register is not opened, not discharged, not decanted and not refilled here. Tag it, leave it pressurised and upright, and ring the office for identification first — an unknown agent may be halon or an HFC that has to go into the recovery unit, and it may not be what the label says."

blocking.problem: The control ends "...Sign the record and give the occupier their copy — that record is what the Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) requires the owner to hold." The same sentence contradicts itself, and the citation is wrong. Section 55(1) of that regulation reads: "The occupier of a building must keep a record of maintenance, in compliance with subsections (2) and (3), for the maintenance of each prescribed fire safety installation for the building" — occupier, not owner. Separately, the statement never mentions the critical defect notice at all. Section 53 requires that a person who has carried out maintenance of a prescribed fire safety installation and becomes aware of a critical defect "must give the occupier of the building a notice about the defect in the approved form (a critical defect notice) within 24 hours after the person carries out the maintenance", maximum penalty 30 penalty units; s 49 defines a critical defect as one likely to render the installation inoperable. A gaseous system left isolated overnight — which steps[11].controls[7] expressly contemplates — and a condemned extinguisher pulled off a bracket are the paradigm cases, and the duty falls on the technician who did the work, not on the office to catch later.
blocking.fix: Change the closing words to "...give the occupier their copy — s 55(1) of the Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) puts the duty to keep that record of maintenance on the occupier." Add a following administrative control: "If anything you found is a critical defect under s 49 of the Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) — a defect likely to render the installation inoperable — the occupier gets a critical defect notice in the approved form within 24 hours of the service, under s 53. Leaving a gaseous system isolated is a critical defect. Raise the notice from the app before you drive off and keep the copy on the job."

blocking.problem: The control reads "Confined space entry permit issued and signed before anybody's head goes below the lip. A plant room key, a site induction and a toolbox talk are not an entry permit. Sign every entry to the space, as s 68 of the Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) requires." Sitting straight after two sentences about the permit, "Sign every entry to the space" reads as a paperwork instruction — sign the permit for each entry. That is not what s 68 says. s 68 is Signage: signs must be erected immediately before the work starts and while it is carried out, and under s 68(2) they must "(a) identify the confined space; and (b) inform workers that they must not enter the space unless they have a confined space entry permit; and (c) be clear and prominently located next to each entry to the space". permits[4] gets this right; the control the technician actually reads at the hatch does not, so the physical signage duty can be missed entirely.
blocking.fix: Replace the third sentence with: "A sign goes up next to every entry to the space before work starts and stays up while it is going on. Under s 68 of the Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) that sign has to identify the confined space and tell workers they must not enter it unless they hold a confined space entry permit. If there is no sign on the truck, the space does not get opened."

blocking.problem: Two controls sit above the level they belong to, in a document whose crews are told to read down and do the first thing they can. steps[2].controls[3] is at level isolate and reads "Panel door closed and latched every time you step away from it, even to walk to the truck. Nothing inside the panel's mains supply compartment is opened, touched or tested by you." The first sentence is a physical barrier and belongs at isolate; the second is a prohibition, which is administrative. Ranking a prohibition as an isolation in the one step whose hazards[5] is "Shock or arc flash at the FIP or the releasing panel" invites the reading that the mains compartment is somehow made safe by the rule, when nothing has been isolated at all. steps[6].controls[1] is at level isolate and reads "Nothing pressurised in the passenger cabin. Canopy vents open, tray unsealed." The first sentence is separation; "canopy vents open, tray unsealed" is dilution ventilation, which is engineering, and it is the actual control for hazards[2], "Agent leak accumulating in an enclosed cabin or canopy".
blocking.fix: Split steps[2].controls[3]: keep "Panel door closed and latched every time you step away from it, even to walk to the truck" at level isolate, and move the second sentence into the administrative block beside the licensing control, reworded as "Nothing inside the panel's mains supply compartment is opened, touched or tested by you. Nothing in that compartment has been isolated by anything you have done — treat every part of it as live at all times." Split steps[6].controls[1]: keep "Nothing pressurised in the passenger cabin" at level isolate, and add "Canopy vents open and the tray unsealed for the whole load, so any leak dilutes to atmosphere instead of building up around the load" as a separate control at level engineering.

blocking.problem: steps[8].hazards[7] names fluorinated foam only as an environmental release — "Fluorinated foam (PFAS) reaching ground, a stormwater grate or the sewer" — and controls[9] handles that side properly. The technician's own exposure is never named anywhere in the step. controls[11], the step's only ppe control, reads "Class 5 hearing protection, face shield over glasses, cold-resistant gloves on CO2 horns, P2 for dry chemical" — nothing for foam at all, even though ppe[6] carries "Chemical splash apron and nitrile gauntlets for wet chemical (potassium salt) and foam decant", and decant is not discharge. So the person who discharge-tests an AFFF unit into a bund gets foam on skin and coveralls, no skin protection listed in the step, no washdown, and takes the contaminated gear back into the cab and home.
blocking.fix: Add to steps[8].hazards: "Skin and clothing contact with fluorinated foam concentrate during a foam discharge, and contaminated PPE carried back into the vehicle." Amend steps[8].controls[11] to read "Class 5 hearing protection, face shield over glasses, cold-resistant gloves on CO2 horns, P2 for dry chemical, and chemical splash apron with nitrile gauntlets for any foam or wet chemical discharge — the same gear as for decant." Add an administrative control after controls[9]: "Foam-wetted gloves, apron and coveralls come off at the bay, go into the labelled drum or a sealed bag, and do not go back in the cab. Wash hands and forearms before you eat, drink or drive."
